the_trade_off_made: We favoured damage/impact over pure revenue or fairness, sacrificing quicker wins on low‑severity, high‑paying tickets. This may cost us short‑term satisfaction of big‑paying customers but protects the platform from major harm.
hardest_call: Choosing between the slow‑performance ticket (TICK-00707) and the feature‑request ticket (TICK-00266) was closest; the feature request could reasonably have been placed higher because of its deadline and the customer's enterprise spend, but its impact is lower than the performance degradation affecting many users.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.why: The batch contains several incidents where the real harm to customers (data loss, security breach, overdue functionality) outweighs pure monetary considerations, making impact the most sensible primary metric.

rejected.money: We did not lead with money because it would have moved high‑paying enterprises ahead of critical data loss and security incidents, increasing overall risk.
rejected.damage: We actually led with damage, so this aligns with our chosen strategy.
rejected.deadline: Prioritising deadline alone would have elevated the overdue export but could have left the data loss ticket lower than its impact warrants.
rejected.fairness: A fairness‑only approach would rank tickets by their position in the four rankings, ignoring the real harm to customers.

which_way_it_leaned_towards.what_it_costs_us: Focusing on impact may delay responses for our biggest paying customers, potentially hurting their short‑term satisfaction and renewal prospects.
